title: The Leaked List
subtitle: A welfare list is online; publishing all of it would prove fairness and expose families
coldOpen: 07:30. A spreadsheet of 900 welfare families appears online.
08:00. Posts claim officials’ relatives are on it.
Families on the list are being named in the street.

briefing.grievance: Residents who were refused help believe the list was rigged for the connected. Families on it are now being harassed. Both groups want the truth, for opposite reasons.
knownFacts: A genuine extract of the list, with names and addresses, is circulating.
The scheme covers 900 families chosen by an income score.
Three families have reported threats since dawn.
unverifiedClaims: A post says forty names belong to officials’ relatives.
A message says the full list will be published by the office at noon.
briefing.responsibility: You run the records office and the scheme. You owe the public fairness and the families their privacy.
briefing.objective: Show how names were chosen without exposing the families further, and stop the harassment.

rightsMoments.question: Refused applicants demand the full list with names and addresses. Must the office publish it to prove fairness?

options.text: No. It should publish the method and audit; the families’ personal data is protected.
options.feedback: Correct. Transparency applies to how decisions are made, not to exposing private individuals.

options.text: Yes. Public money means every recipient must be publicly named with an address.
options.feedback: Public accountability does not require publishing addresses that put families at risk.

options.text: Yes, but only the names, not the addresses.
options.feedback: Names alone still expose families to harassment; the method and audit answer the fairness question.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 21 protects privacy and dignity. Accountability for public money is met by publishing the rules, the audit and the appeals route, not private data.
rightsMoments.why: Families were being harassed at their doors; the audit answered the fairness question without adding to that harm.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: Must the office publish every name and address to prove the list was fair?

options.a: No. Publish the rule and the audit. Keep people’s details private.
options.b: Yes. Public money means every name and address must be public.

feedback.a: Yes! Show how choices were made, not who the families are.
feedback.b: No. Addresses put families in danger.
feedback.c: Names still expose families. The rule and audit are enough.

simple.principle: People have a right to privacy. Show how a decision was made, not private details.
simple.why: Families were being bullied at their doors. The audit proved fairness without hurting them.

closing.good: The rule was public, the names stayed private, and the people who leaked the list are the ones being looked for.
closing.mixed: The audit answered the crowd, but a few families are still waiting for the knocking to stop.
closing.poor: The office finished what the leak started, and the families on the list will remember who read their names.
